chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, who said:

A son of Jaʿfar became gravely ill while Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was sitting to one side. Whenever a person came near him, he would say: “Do not touch him, for he only increases in weakness, and he is at his weakest in this state; and whoever touches him in this state has assisted against him.”

So when the boy passed away, he gave orders concerning him, and his eyes were closed and his jaw was bound. Then he said: “We may grieve so long as the command of Allah has not descended; but when the command of Allah descends, then nothing remains for us except submission.”

Then he called for oil and applied it, and used kohl, and called for food, so he and those with him ate. Then he said: “This is beautiful patience.” Then he gave orders concerning him, so he was given ghusl, and he wore a khazz robe, a khazz cloak, and a khazz turban, and went out and performed salat over him.

key_terms.أَمْرُ اللَّهِ: the divine command or decree of Allah in the matter of death
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمُ: submission and acceptance of Allah’s decree
key_terms.الصَّبْرُ الْجَمِيلُ: beautiful patience, marked by dignified endurance and acceptance
key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: the young boy who passed away
key_terms.ثَقُلَ: became gravely ill or burdened by severe sickness
key_terms.فَصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: he performed salat over him, the funeral prayer
key_terms.فَغُسِّلَ: he was given ghusl, the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: How did Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام teach patience and proper conduct at the time of death?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the conduct of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام during the final illness and death of a child from the family. It shows both practical actions around a dying person and the spiritual etiquette of grieving before death, then submitting fully once the divine decree has come. It also highlights "beautiful patience" through composed acceptance without denying natural sorrow.
